items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' after the greeting
Gave the agenda statement about the 10-minute questionnaire but never asked an explicit 'Sound good?' -- just moved ahead when Alan said 'Yup'
Never asked about stairs, floors, or elevator access at the destination (Oakwell Court apartment, unit 726) despite this being a move-in to an apartment
Never asked about access concerns -- parking, HOA restrictions, or walk distance from the truck to the unit
Never asked a moving-stressors question (e.g. 'anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
Never mentioned the No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) even though the move includes a couch and bed frame being unloaded
Meet Your Mover (advance email with mover photo/info) was never mentioned
On-Time Guarantee (discount if the arrival window is missed) was never mentioned
Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped entirely -- no consolidation tips (boxes, loose items) and no 'take a carload' suggestion
Never explicitly asked to lock in the booking on the call -- let Alan end the call by just asking for the quote to be emailed
Didn't mention replying to the email with corrections, or give business hours / how to reach the branch
Didn't ask 'Any other questions before I let you go?' before ending the call
Never used the customer's name (Alan) at any point during the call
top_strength: Garrison gave a clear, confident, and accurate pricing walkthrough -- the $96/mover/hour rate, the 2.5-hour minimum, the exact $480 total, and no-hidden-fees policy -- and proactively offered to use any leftover minimum time on furniture reassembly.
coaching_note: This was a move-in to apartment unit 726, but Garrison never asked about stairs, elevator, or parking access -- build a quick access question into every intake, and layer in the missing differentiators (No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) and the Save Your Ass prep tips before the call ends.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and affirming throughout ('gotcha,' 'perfect,' 'alrighty') but transactional -- no use of the customer's name and little acknowledgment beyond confirming details, though Alan stayed satisfied through the close.
